label: PF Backlog 672
title: Mandatory implementation controls and tech-stack readiness gates
body:
Enforce production-readiness inputs as executable gates, not documentation placeholders.

Pre-code (Gate 1):
- design_pack.implementation_controls: AC/FR -> control -> planned code symbol -> positive test -> negative/failure test -> tenant/RLS test -> concurrency test -> observability -> evidence.
- functional_spec traceability per FR: code owner, positive test, negative test, tenant/RLS test, concurrency test, observability signal.
- tech-stack checklist: Go fmt/vet/race/context/connection reuse/error classification; PostgreSQL transactions/constraints/RLS/migrations/backup; object store tenant scope/refs/hash/atomicity/GC; API auth/validation/tenant/failure; config enum fail-closed.
- red tests written before implementation for negative, failure, tenant isolation, concurrency and observability.

During code:
- no caller-controlled security inputs (paths, DSNs, tenant IDs, roles);
- one owner per concern; reuse existing stores/adapters;
- instrument every failure mode with owner/threshold.

Post-code/precheck:
- implementation_readiness_check.py validates actual symbols/tests/evidence and rejects missing/dead/placeholder controls;
- integration/RLS/race tests; migration up/down/backup check; self-review removes dead code, duplicate logic and unused paths.

Merge gate:
- Gate 2.5 receives implementation_controls and verifies planned-vs-actual coverage;
- no merge with missing controls/tests/evidence;
- escaped defects require RCCA + new backlog item, never a silent cross-PR fix.

Mandatory implementation prompt/gate:
- Before editing, produce the 360-degree implementation plan: each AC/FR/control mapped to code symbol, happy path, negative/failure, tenant/RLS, concurrency/race, config invalid, data/IO atomicity, migration/rollback, resource/connection reuse, observability, and evidence test.
- Write failing tests first for negative, tenant, race, config and observability cases; no happy-path-only implementation.
- Forbid caller-controlled security inputs (paths, DSNs, tenant/role, limits) and silent fallbacks; invalid config must fail closed.
- Reuse existing owners; no duplicate store/bus/DB stacks; no dead code or uncalled controls.
- After coding, self-review the diff against the plan and delete unneeded code; then run unit + integration/RLS/race tests.
- Gate 2.5 reviews planned-vs-actual coverage; any missing row blocks merge.
- Any escaped defect requires RCCA and a new backlog item, never a silent follow-up patch.

## Design (pending HIL approval)
Artifact: docs/IMPLEMENTATION-CONTROLS-DESIGN.md
- Canonical design_pack.implementation_controls rows: AC, kind, control, symbol, positive/negative/tenant/concurrency tests, observability, evidence.
- Reuse existing owners: design_pack.py, Gate 1, architect_review.py (Gate 2.5), gate2_completion_check.py.
- New implementation_readiness_check.py for pre-code and final-diff verification.
- New operator-only POST /api/v1/backlog/items/{id}/design-pack via core.backlog.update.
- RCCA rule for escaped defects; no silent cross-PR fixes.

## Reconciliation
PRIOR DECISIONS: BI-PF-1243; BI-PF-1469/1470 Gate 2; BI-PF-1536; BI-PF-1537 rejected; BI-PF-1268 RCCA.
EXISTING PATH: design_pack.py, templates, gate1_check.py, architect_review.py, gate2_completion_check.py, core.backlog.
ASSUMPTIONS: new items only; no retrofitting; tooling is Python/JSON/Markdown; no new runtime store.
DIVERGENCES: backlog API has no design-pack write endpoint today; BI-PF-1538 must add it before API-only enforcement.
OPEN QUESTIONS: enforcement cutoff; MINOR blocking; exact symbol resolution; escaped-defect metric owner.

## Impact review
| Area | Impact | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Language | Python tooling/templates/API; no runtime Go | language_check |
| API | New design-pack write endpoint | api_check + tests |
| AC-1 | Matrix required at Gate 1 | gate tests |
| AC-2 | Readiness checker pre-code + final | checker tests |
| AC-3 | Templates + Gate 2.5 + RCCA | prompt/gate tests |
| Data | Backlog fields only | store registry review |
| Security | Operator-only API | API tests |


## Design amendment: mandatory prompts and delivery states
- Design/functional-spec five mandates are now required template sections and Gate 1 checks.
- Implementation five mandates are now required Gate 2.5 evidence.
- Delivery states are explicit: Code, Integration, Validation, Quality Approved, Delivery Complete; only Delivery Complete satisfies Gate 2/merge.
- Coding and tech-stack guidelines are mapped to executable checks/evidence, not prose; readiness fails when a required check is missing, unrun or unrecorded.

brief.problem: Implementation prompts lack 360-degree controls and permit happy-path-only work.
brief.what_adds: Prompt mandates, item control matrix, executable readiness checks and API write path.
brief.why: BI-PF-1268 showed reviews were the first quality gate and fixes introduced regressions.

objective: Prevent happy-path-only implementation and fix-induced regressions by making every AC/control, test, tenant/RLS, concurrency, migration, resource and observability case explicit and verifiable before and after code.
acceptance_criteria: Gate 1 blocks unless every AC/FR has an implementation_controls row with code symbol, positive, negative/failure, tenant/RLS, concurrency, observability and evidence mappings.
implementation_readiness_check runs before code and against the final diff, verifying actual symbols, tests, evidence, tech-stack checks, migration/backup and no caller-controlled security inputs.
Templates and Gate 2.5 consume the same implementation-controls matrix; no merge with missing or dead controls, and escaped defects require RCCA plus a new backlog item.

Design and functional-spec templates must enforce the five mandate areas and Gate 1 must reject missing requirement analysis, complete functional/technical design, 360-degree scenarios/impact, implementation/validation readiness and independent completeness review.
Every item must report Code Complete, Integration Complete, Validation Complete, Quality Approved and Delivery Complete separately; Gate 2 and merge must require evidenced Delivery Complete.

Coding and tech-stack guidelines must be mapped in config/implementation-controls.json to executable checks and evidence, with implementation_readiness_check failing on missing, unrun or unrecorded checks.
in_scope: Templates, config checklist, tests, RCCA rule
approach: Add a design_pack.implementation_controls matrix and enforce it through existing design_pack, Gate 1, Gate 2.5, completion and merge owners. Add implementation_readiness_check.py for pre-code and final-diff verification, one operator-only design-pack API write endpoint, template sections, and an RCCA rule. No runtime store or duplicate gate engine.
risks: Path-only checks give false confidence; require symbol and test/evidence resolution in final mode.
Retrofitting historical items; enforce by creation cutoff only.
Template/checker drift; use one schema validator.
Gate latency; cache parsing and scan only changed files.
Over-blocking trivial work; allow explicit N/A reasons.
rollback: Remove the design-pack API endpoint, checker wiring, template sections and control enforcement; retain the design doc and RCCA history. No data migration to reverse.
